source.citation: Zhu J, Ogden FL, Lai W, Chen X, Talbot CA (2016), An explicit approach to capture diffusive effects in finite water-content method for solving vadose zone flow, Journal of Hydrology 535:270-281

source_bound_findings: the paper explicitly adds soil-water diffusive effects to the earlier finite-water-content / Talbot-Ogden method
advection and diffusion are treated separately per water-content bin
conductivity and diffusivity are treated as bin-dependent constants during each local analytical calculation
diffusive water ahead of the advective front is calculated and redistributed among bins
the added diffusion treatment uses algebraic calculations rather than a global nonlinear Richards solve
the authors report material improvement in water-content profile shape while total and cumulative infiltration differ little from the original advective method in their tests
published horizontal-infiltration tests used 200 water-content bins and time steps ranging from about 0.005 h for sand to 0.2 h for clay

qualification_consequence.previous_binary_assumption: FWC must either neglect the SMVE diffusion-like term or revert to full Richards
qualification_consequence.corrected_position: A third candidate exists: bounded explicit per-bin diffusion correction. It must be assessed separately because it can improve profile fidelity without a global Newton solve.

new_candidate_families.name: FWC_ADVECTIVE
new_candidate_families.physics: gravity plus integrated capillary/advection-like term; no explicit diffusion-like correction
new_candidate_families.expected_strength: low algorithmic complexity and sharp-front handling
new_candidate_families.primary_risk: profile-shape bias when diffusion is material

new_candidate_families.name: FWC_EXPLICIT_DIFFUSION
new_candidate_families.physics: FWC advection plus explicit binwise diffusion redistribution
new_candidate_families.expected_strength: closer profile representation without global nonlinear iteration
primary_risks: small stable time steps may be required
redistribution/event work must remain strictly conservative
state and scratch layout may be expensive for hundreds of thousands of columns

runtime_and_state_gate_additions: measure accuracy and cost versus number of water-content bins, including 16, 32, 64, 128 and the published 200-bin scale where feasible
measure maximum stable/admitted internal step count separately for sand, loam and clay
separate persistent front/bin state from worker-local diffusion scratch
prove that diffusive redistribution conserves the exact accepted-step water ledger to roundoff
characterize whether the diffusion correction is vectorizable over fixed-bin templates
do not assume the published 200-bin configuration is an acceptable MultiSWAP production layout
applicability_implication: The neglected-diffusion issue is no longer by itself a reason to reject FWC. Instead it creates a two-level applicability/cost study: advective FWC may qualify where diffusion is demonstrably negligible, while explicit-diffusion FWC may extend the envelope only if its bin and substep costs remain bounded and acceptable.
